paper_metadata.title: Unsupervised Quantum Anomaly Detection on Noisy Quantum Processors

summary: The paper studies a 10-qubit projected quantum-kernel one-class SVM for credit-card fraud anomaly detection on a synthetic Sparkov dataset, using three hardware-efficient feature maps (qrbf-CX, qrbf-ECR, qrbf-RXX). In simulation, the qrbf-OCSVM achieves F1 scores above 0.9 for anomaly ratios below 5×10^-2 and, at r=0.2, beats the classical rbf-OCSVM with estimated probabilities of 69.2%, 74.7%, and 64.8% across the three feature maps; on hardware, tomography precision saturates beyond about 10^3 shots and a 10^5-shot run took 2.5 hours on IBM Falcon r2.

experiments.description: Projected quantum-kernel one-class SVM anomaly detection on a synthetic credit-card fraud dataset, evaluated in simulation across three hardware-efficient feature maps (qrbf-CX, qrbf-ECR, qrbf-RXX) and compared against a classical rbf-OCSVM baseline.

algorithm.variant: Projected quantum kernel OCSVM (qrbf-OCSVM) with hardware-efficient feature maps

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each 20-dimensional sample is encoded into a hardware-efficient quantum circuit using single-qubit RX and RZ rotations; entangling gates depend on the feature map (CX, ECR, or RXX). Projected quantum kernels are computed from one-qubit reduced density matrices obtained via partial state tomography.
problem_formulation.objective_function: One-class SVM objective minimizing 1/2 ||w||^2 - ρ + (1/(νl)) Σ_i ξ_i subject to w^T φ(x_i) ≥ ρ - ξ_i and ξ_i ≥ 0; kernelized dual uses projected quantum kernel K_γ(x_i,x_j)=exp(-γ Σ_k ||ρ_k(x_i)-ρ_k(x_j)||_F^2).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Standard OCSVM slack variables and ν-constraint; no additional quantum constraints.

problem_instance.description: Unsupervised anomaly detection for financial fraud on a feature-engineered Sparkov credit-card transaction dataset.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Sparkov credit card transactions fraud dataset

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic credit-card transaction data generated by Sparkov; 2019-2020, 1,000 customers and 800 merchants, 1,852,394 total samples, 9,651 fraud transactions (~0.52%). Feature-engineered to 21 variables including label; experiments use 20 features for encoding.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Feature engineering included fraud-rate encoding for categorical variables, binary gender dummies, dropping unused variables, and selecting a 20-dimensional feature set for quantum encoding. Train/test split used 9:1 in simulations and 450/50 for hardware benchmark at r=0.2.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation: 10-fold cross-validation and repeated dataset splits (10 splits) for r=0.2; hardware: single experimental execution per backend with F1 score on train and test, plus 128 repeated simulator runs to estimate standard deviation.

noise_model.noise_type: finite-sampling noise in simulation; hardware noise on QPUs

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Native gate sets of IBM, IonQ, and AQT hardware; feature maps restricted to single-qubit gates and nearest-neighbor two-qubit gates where applicable
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature engineering on Sparkov data; grid search for ν and γ; 5-fold cross-validation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: F1 score computation; probability that qrbf outperforms classical rbf estimated from truncated normal model.

speedup_claims.conditions: Empirical generalization comparison on the Sparkov fraud dataset; no asymptotic speedup analysis provided.
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports better generalization/F1 for qrbf-OCSVM in some regimes, but does not claim computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 10-qubit hardware-efficient feature maps; 200 shots in the tomography protocol; 10-fold CV and 10 repeated dataset splits for r=0.2
limiting_factors: Classical rbf-OCSVM baseline is explicitly compared and often matched or outperformed in the paper's own discussion
No asymptotic speedup or crossover analysis is provided
Performance depends on noisy projected kernels and partial tomography
The paper reports empirical generalization, not computational advantage

notes: num_qubits inferred as 10 from Appendix A feature maps showing q0 through q9, i.e. 10 qubits.
hardware.type set to simulator_other for the simulation portion of the experiment; the paper also reports real QPU runs separately in exp_2.
circuit depth not explicitly quantified; only shallow/hardware-efficient feature maps are described.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided; only empirical generalization comparisons are reported.

The paper reports that qrbf-OCSVM often outperforms the classical rbf-OCSVM on test F1, with estimated win probabilities of 69.2%, 74.7%, and 64.8% for qrbf-CX, qrbf-ECR, and qrbf-RXX respectively at r=0.2.
However, this is an empirical generalization comparison, not a demonstrated quantum advantage in runtime or scaling.

experiments.description: Partial state tomography of single-qubit states |+> and |T> on IBM Falcon r2 superconducting hardware, compared against a finite-sampling simulator.

algorithm.variant: Partial state tomography / shadow tomography benchmark

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Single-qubit state preparation and Pauli-basis measurement for tomography; no optimization problem.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the one-qubit reduced density matrix ρ from randomized Pauli measurements and compare to the ideal state via Frobenius norm distance.

problem_instance.description: Tomography benchmark on prepared single-qubit states |+> and |T>.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Repeated tomography experiments 100 times per shot count to estimate variance.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Distance d(ρ,ρ_exp) measured versus number of shots; repeated 100 times for each shot count.

noise_model.mitigation_details: No mitigation; precision saturates on hardware due to calibration drift over long runtimes.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute Frobenius norm distance between ideal and experimental density matrices.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Distance decreases with shots on simulator; saturates on hardware beyond ~10^3 shots.

speedup_claims.conditions: Tomography benchmark on simulator vs IBM Falcon r2 hardware.
speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim; hardware precision saturates beyond about 10^3 shots due to calibration drift.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 1 qubit; tomography repeated 100 times per shot count; up to 10^5 shots; 2.5 hours runtime at 10^5 shots
limiting_factors: No quantum-vs-classical advantage claim is made
The experiment measures tomography precision only
Hardware calibration drift limits precision at high shot counts

notes: The paper explicitly states preparation of single-qubit states on a Falcon r2 QPU by IBM Quantum.
Circuit depth is not numerically reported; tomography circuits are shallow single-qubit basis-rotation circuits.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided.
The paper benchmarks partial state tomography on IBM Falcon r2 and compares it to a finite-sampling simulator.
This is a methodological benchmark, not an advantage demonstration.

speedup_claims.conditions: Hardware benchmark of qrbf-OCSVM on AQT Ibex, IonQ Harmony, and IBM superconducting devices.
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports generalization enhancement on QPUs despite noise, but no computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 10-qubit feature maps; real QPUs (AQT Ibex, IonQ Harmony, IBM Eagle r2/r3 and Falcon r2); 450/50 train-test split at r=0.2; 200 shots
limiting_factors: Only small-scale QPU runs are reported
